title: Stop Loss & Take Profit
hook: Protect your capital first. Always know your exit before your entry.
mission: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to place a stop loss based on structure, not comfort.

blocks.heading: Your stop loss belongs where the setup is proven wrong

beats.heading: Not a random distance
beats.body: In an uptrend, that's below the swing low — not some random number of points away, and not just wherever feels comfortable.

beats.heading: A planned exit
beats.body: A take profit is a planned exit, not something you decide in the moment based on fear or greed.

blocks.heading: What's the risk in her approach?
blocks.scenario: A trader places her stop loss "a comfortable distance" below her entry rather than below the actual swing low.

options.label: It's disconnected from the point where the trade idea is actually proven wrong
options.feedback: Right — a comfort-based stop might get hit by normal noise, or fail to protect her at all.

options.label: There's no risk — comfort is a valid distance
options.feedback: Comfort isn't a structural reason for a stop's placement.

blocks.heading: Follow the trade
sequence: Price pulls back and gets close to the stop, without closing below the swing low
blocks.askAfter: Price pulls back and gets close to the stop, without closing below the swing low
blocks.prompt: Fear kicks in — should the stop move closer to "reduce risk"?

options.label: No — moving it early abandons the actual invalidation point
options.feedback: Right — your stop protects the plan; moving it out of fear defeats its purpose.

options.label: Yes — tightening it feels safer
options.feedback: Tightening a stop based on fear usually gets you stopped out of a trade that was still valid.

blocks.quote: Your stop loss protects your account and your structure logic — it isn't punishment, and it isn't about ego.

questions.question: In an uptrend, where should your stop loss usually go?
options: A random number of points away
questions.why: That's the point where the uptrend idea is actually proven wrong.

questions.question: After entry, discipline means you ___ to the plan instead of moving your stop out of fear.
questions.why: Committing to the plan is what makes a stop loss actually work.

takeaways: A stop loss belongs where the setup is actually proven wrong, not wherever feels comfortable.
Moving your stop out of fear defeats the reason it exists.
A take profit is planned in advance, not decided in the moment.
remember: Your stop protects the plan — not your feelings in the moment.
